title: Nashville Trivia Night

questions.q: Which weekly country music radio show, first broadcast in 1925, is Nashville's most famous?
Nashville's full-scale replica of an ancient Greek temple stands in which park?
Nashville hot chicken is traditionally served on white bread and topped with what?
The Nashville Predators' logo comes from the fossil of which prehistoric animal, dug up under downtown Nashville in 1971?
Before moving to Tennessee, the Titans were known as the Houston what?
Which Nashville university's sports teams are called the Commodores?
President Andrew Jackson's plantation home outside Nashville is known by what name?
The Jubilee Singers began touring in 1871 to raise money for which Nashville university?
The cluster of record labels and publishers around 16th and 17th Avenues is known by what two-word name?
Nashville's downtown strip of honky-tonks runs along the lower end of which street?

notes: First broadcast 28 November 1925 on WSM as the WSM Barn Dance; see Grand Ole Opry (Wikipedia) or opry.com history.
The Parthenon, built for the 1897 Tennessee Centennial Exposition, in Centennial Park; see Parthenon (Nashville) (Wikipedia) or nashvilleparthenon.com.
Hot chicken is served on white bread with pickle chips; see Hot chicken (Wikipedia).
Smilodon skeleton found downtown in 1971 during construction.
Houston Oilers moved to Tennessee in 1997, renamed Titans in 1999; see Tennessee Titans (Wikipedia).
Vanderbilt University athletics are the Commodores; see Vanderbilt Commodores (Wikipedia) or vucommodores.com.
The Hermitage, Jackson's home in the Hermitage area of Davidson County; see The Hermitage (Nashville, Tennessee) (Wikipedia) or thehermitage.com.
Fisk Jubilee Singers first toured in October 1871 to raise funds for Fisk University; see Fisk Jubilee Singers (Wikipedia).
Music Row, centred on 16th and 17th Avenues South; see Music Row (Wikipedia).
Lower Broadway honky-tonk district downtown; see Lower Broadway (Wikipedia) or visitmusiccity.com.
